text: The spirometry shows reduced FVC and FEV1 with a normal ratio, which suggests a restrictive lung pattern rather than the obstruction seen in typical bronchitis. Given your chronic cough, 11-year history, and non-smoker status, do you have a history of dust inhalation, acid reflux, or other respiratory symptoms like hemoptysis?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Aggressive cough with thick, yellow-green sputum. I also have Cough worse in the morning, History of recurrent bronchitis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis. The combination of an 11-year history of chronic cough with copious, purulent (yellow-green) sputum, morning exacerbations, and recurrent "bronchitis" requiring antibiotics in a non-smoker is classic for bronchiectasis. The spirometry findings (reduced volumes with a normal ratio) suggest a mixed or restrictive pattern often seen with significant airway damage, while the normal IgE and eosinophils rule out asthma. Please proceed to obtain a High-Resolution CT (HRCT) of the chest to confirm the diagnosis.
